name: SiegeWeaponSpot - Default (seed v1)
description: A place reserved for a siege weapon in a scenario, owned by one team. Created from the scenario's Siege weapons step.

steps.description: Name the spot and pick the team it belongs to.

fields.label: Scenario
fields.description: Filled in from the scenario you are editing.

fields.label: Team
fields.description: Only this team can place a weapon here. Attackers and defenders can both have spots.

fields.label: Name
fields.description: Shown in the spot picker, e.g. 'North wall tower'.

fields.label: Order
fields.description: Leave empty to add it after the existing spots.

steps.description: Where the weapon goes. Send the task on Min X to Minecraft and claim it in game: it reads a WorldEdit selection or WorldGuard region, takes the facing from your look direction (you can change it) and fills the bounds, facing, size class and region here (needs siege.weapons.enabled on the game server). You can also type or correct them; with bounds the size class is worked out from them and the facing on save.

fields.label: Facing
fields.description: The direction the weapon points; it is rotated to face this way.

fields.label: Size class
fields.description: The largest weapon class that fits: Small 7 x 9 x 5, Medium 7 x 9 x 8, Large 9 x 15 x 16 (width across x length along the facing x height). With all six bounds the API works it out from them and the facing; bounds smaller than Small are refused.

fields.label: WorldGuard region
fields.description: Optional: the region the spot was taken from.

fields.label: Min X
fields.description: Selection corner; give all six coordinates or none. Capturing in Minecraft fills all six, the facing, the size class and the region, and shows warnings for a floor that isn't solid or a volume that isn't clear.

fields.label: Max X
fields.description: Opposite corner; each max must be at least its min.
